A recurrence rule describes a repeating pattern of times. Recurrences rules in SavvyCal are modeled
after the conventions of [iCalendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICalendar) recurrence rules (RRULE),

anyOf.description:
Server-computed workflow state for a booking intent. Provides step routing,
completability, and defunct state so the frontend can render the correct
booking flow without inferring these from raw fields.

available_steps.description: Ordered list of steps the user can visit. Computed from service forms and locked_fields.

can_change_slot.description: Whether slot fields (start_at, end_at, time_zone) are unlocked and can be modified.

can_complete.description: Whether the intent has enough valid data to submit right now. When true, calling the complete endpoint will succeed regardless of whether the current status is pending or slot_selected.

defunct_reason.description: Why the intent is defunct. Null when not defunct.

is_defunct.description: Whether the intent is in an unrecoverable state and should render a terminal UI.

resume_step.description: The step the UI should show on load or resume. One of: booking, info, form:<form_id>, confirmed, defunct.

anyOf.title: BookingIntentWorkflow

workflow.description: Server-computed workflow state. Present on single-intent responses, null on list responses.
